name: Login Brush
author: chitvan

sections.description:
Login Brush provides administrator controls for the login page background, logo, form, labels, input fields, focus, placeholder color, button, links, messages and Remember Me label.

The editor includes a WordPress Media Library picker and desktop, tablet and mobile preview widths. Draft settings are not published until saved with customization enabled. The preview is a protected, inert specimen built with WordPress’s form API, rather than a functioning authentication form. It does not accept credentials or reproduce third-party authentication widgets or every native screen. The actual login page remains the final appearance reference.

Login Brush changes presentation only. WordPress continues to handle authentication, password resets, registration, cookies and redirects. No custom CSS, external fonts, telemetry or external API services are included. Selected media may be served from the site’s configured media host.

Keyboard focus indicators and native controls are preserved. Administrators remain responsible for choosing readable colors and suitable text sizes. Checkbox accent color is a browser-dependent enhancement; core checkbox rendering can limit its effect. Custom login-button labels use a wrapping submit button with the native form name/value and attributes preserved. Uncustomized native login buttons remain unchanged. Extensions that require an input tag rather than a button need compatibility verification; unexpected or ambiguous markup is left unchanged.

Settings are per site. Deactivation preserves them. Deleting the plugin through WordPress removes Login Brush settings, including per-site settings on multisite, while preserving media and user content. Multisite cleanup still needs release verification on a representative network.

Author: Chitvan (WordPress.org contributor chitvan). Requires WordPress 6.5 or later and PHP 8.2 or later. Broader browser, assistive-technology and hosting compatibility remains subject to verification. No WordPress.org approval is claimed.
sections.installation:
1. Install the Login Brush plugin directory in wp-content/plugins and activate it through Plugins.
  2. Open Login Brush > Customize as a user with manage_options.
  3. Choose settings and inspect the draft preview.
  4. Enable customization and save changes to publish the design.
  5. Verify the native login page while logged out.
sections.faq:
How are footer-link colors handled?

With a selected background color, empty link colors use black or white when inherited core colors would fall below 4.5:1. Inherited hover colors also receive an underline, and keyboard focus retains a contrasting outline. Explicit link colors are preserved. Background images and user-selected colors require manual contrast review; this fallback does not guarantee accessibility for every design.

Does this replace WordPress authentication?

No. It customizes the existing interface without changing authentication behavior.

Are draft preview changes saved automatically?

No. Preview requests validate drafts without persisting them. Use Save Changes to publish.

Why can I not type credentials or follow links in the preview?

The preview is deliberately inert. Test authentication only on the actual WordPress login page.

What happens when I reset or delete the plugin?

Reset removes saved customization. Deactivation retains settings. Uninstall removes Login Brush settings and preserves attachments and users.
